meta.title: 04 Interviews — FDE + GenAI / Agentic AI
meta.purpose: Sourced research notes for an FDE and GenAI/Agentic AI interview handbook

labeling_rules.official_verified: Published by the employer on careers, official interview guides, hiring blogs, or official PDFs. Process can still vary by team.
labeling_rules.candidate_reported: Prep-site compilations, Glassdoor, coaching platforms. Useful for round flavor; not company policy.
labeling_rules.unverified_rumor: Circulating numbers or hidden-filter claims without a primary source. Must not be presented as confirmed process.

standing_caveats: AI-tool policy differs by company and by round; ask the recruiter.
FDE is a family of titles; confirm employer and title before prepping.
Repeated 2026 FDE-blog claims of ~40% decomposition pass rate and ~30% weight are not independently verified.

leetcode_justification.summary: Classic SWE at Google/Meta/Amazon still justifies heavy LeetCode. FDE justifies medium practical coding plus decomposition. Lab GenAI SWE justifies practical multi-part coding, tests, LLM systems, and mission literacy more than LeetCode hard.

by_track.notes: Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft official technical pages still center DSA, complexity, and (Microsoft) runnable code plus testing. NVIDIA uses HackerRank coding as a floor plus domain.

Palantir/Databricks/Scale FDE coding is commonly LeetCode-medium dressed as workflows (SQL, APIs, messy data). Decomposition, learning, debugging, and customer communication decide more offers than hard DP.

OpenAI official bar is design quality, code quality, performance, test coverage. Anthropic official: look-up allowed, stdlib fluency required. Candidate reports: progressive specs, concurrency, LLM serving design, values.

companies.name: Palantir

stages.name: Phone interviews
stages.notes: Background, experiences, interest. Engineering roles include a coding question. Official tips: think out loud, ask questions, start simple then expand.

stages.name: Onsite
stages.format: in-person or virtual, personalized to skillset and role (FDSE vs SWE)
stages.notes: Discuss accomplishments and failures; ask clarifying questions on analytical/technical problems. Recruiter provides prep material.

official_process.ai_policy: Not stated on the official getting-hired pages fetched. Candidate reports say Palantir FDE interviews prohibit AI.

stages.name: Technical screen
stages.format: HackerRank ~90 min coding+SQL+API or live CodePair/Karat ~60 min

stages.name: Onsite pool of 3x60 min
stages.notes: Decomposition nearly universal. ~15-20 min behavioral embedded in each round.

stages.name: Hiring manager
stages.notes: Often re-tests a weak onsite area; team matching.

candidate_reported.coding_difficulty: LeetCode medium framed as a real workflow, not LeetCode-hard graphs/DP
candidate_reported.ai_policy: Prohibited throughout FDE loop (Aced candidate-updated guide)

emphasis.fde: decomposition, communication, why Palantir, practical coding
emphasis.genai: Forward Deployed AI Engineer title exists on careers; loop not separately published

gaps: Official pages do not name decomposition/learning/re-engineering. Treat those as candidate-reported names for official competencies.

companies.name: Databricks

stages: Pre-onsite screen (HM, technical assessment, or skill evaluation)
official_process.format: Virtual Google Meet unless recruiter specifies otherwise
official_process.coding_bar_official: Production-quality code, tests, edge cases, Big-O. Language-agnostic but fluency required.

stages.name: Decomposition
stages.notes: Vague business goal to KPI, data, app layer, optional AI

candidate_reported_fde.notes: FDE org launch-in-2026 is a prep-site claim; confirm live JDs. Some loops add take-home or presentation. Hiring committee can still no-hire.

gaps: Official engineering PDF is SWE-shaped; FDE-specific round list is candidate-reported.

companies.name: OpenAI
roles: Forward Deployed Engineer (title exists; loop not on official guide)

official_process.philosophy: Not credential-driven. Collaboration, communication, feedback, mission alignment.

stages.name: Skills-based assessment
stages.notes: Varies by team; may be more than one; recruiting provides prep.

official_process.ai_policy: Varies by interview. Some formats allow AI tools; others assess independent problem-solving. Recruiter materials specify. Ask if unsure.

notes: Decentralized; recruiter is source of truth.
Coding more practical than stock LeetCode; multi-part; sometimes information theory/probability.
Onsite may include slides presentation of a past hard project.
Agentic coding round in beta: existing codebase plus authorized agent.
Paid 48h work trial is team-dependent and conflicting across blogs; official guide only says take-homes may occur.
FDE flavor (not official): RAG/evals/tool-use design and customer-pitch round.

gaps: No official FDE-specific loop on the interview guide.
Work-trial reports conflict.

companies.name: Anthropic
roles: Applied AI Engineer (closest public FDE analog; loop not published)

highlights: What you can do, not where you learned it.
About half of technical staff had no prior ML.
If engineering background, apply as engineer.
Technical: Colab and CodeSignal; looking things up allowed; stdlib fluency required.
Re-apply after 12 months or sooner if material change.

ai_policy.resume: Draft yourself, then refine with Claude.

stages: Recruiter 30 min — mission alignment is a real filter
Coding challenge 60-90 min live or CodeSignal take-home, progressive spec, not stock LeetCode
Onsite: coding, system design, second coding, company values; HM before or inside onsite
candidate_reported.values_round: Often described as the hardest; personal/ethical; they want skepticism not enthusiasm. Suggested reading: Machines of Loving Grace; The Adolescence of Technology; Core Views on AI Safety.

gaps: No official FDE/Applied AI round list.

companies.name: Google
roles: Cloud/applied AI customer roles (FDE analog, loop not official)

highlights: Apply to at most three jobs per 30 days.
Typical onsite 3-4 interviews in one day.
Four attributes commonly cited: GCA, RRK, Leadership, Googleyness.
Hiring committee reviews written feedback; then team match.

stages: Loop: 2-4 coding, code comprehension or AI-assisted code comprehension (select US teams, 2026), systems architecture for experienced, Googleyness

gaps: No official Google FDE loop page found.

official_process.loop_size_official: Most interviews include 2-4 conversations up to an hour each.
official_process.coding: Language you are strong in; no pseudocode; third-party tool that runs code; test before done.
official_process.algorithms: Recursion; at least one n log n sort; Big-O.
official_process.ai_ml: Role-dependent: models, training pipelines, evaluation, applying AI/ML algorithms.
official_process.ai_policy: Responsible AI in prep allowed; no outside assistance during assessments/interviews unless explicitly permitted.

candidate_reported.notes: Senior SWE loops often 4-5 rounds including an As-Appropriate senior interviewer. AA is widely reported but not named on the current public how-we-hire page.

companies.name: Amazon
roles: AWS ProServe / prototyping / GenAI specialist (FDE analog)

loop.bar_raiser: Interviewer from outside the hiring team; maintains hiring bar.
loop.technical_share: Technical roles dedicate approximately half the process to technical assessments.
loop.behavioral: STAR; I not we; metrics; Leadership Principles throughout.

leadership_principles: Strive to be Earth’s Best Employer
Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility
sde_topics: general machine learning and artificial intelligence

candidate_reported.notes: Each interviewer assigned 2-3 LPs. Some engineering loops may include a GenAI fluency round; not named on the official SDE topics page.

ai_native.notes: Many interviews include a built-in AI assistant in CoderPad. Candidates are expected to use it. Outside AI unauthorized. Models include Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Meta models. Design interviews use CoderPad plus Mermaid Markdown. Languages: Python, Java, TypeScript, C++, C#, Kotlin, Swift, Rust, Go.

candidate_reported.mid_level_onsite: two coding, one-two design, one behavioral
candidate_reported.leetcode: Still justified for speed and the non-AI coding round; also practice directing an in-environment agent.

stages: Search and apply (focus on top 3-5 roles)
Phone/video/in-person with HM, teammates, other groups
Onsite in-person interview required before an offer
Technical coding exercise usually HackerRank on provided whiteboard or laptop
official_process.ai_policy: Use of unapproved outside tools such as ChatGPT during the interview results in disqualification.
official_process.insider_chat: Optional 15-min CRG conversation; does not influence hiring.

candidate_reported.notes: Highly team-specific. Mix of LeetCode medium, C++/memory, CUDA/GPU domain, systems. Timeline commonly 6-8 weeks.

companies.name: Scale AI

official_process.notes: Job postings exist. No public round-by-round interview guide found on scale.com as of 2026-09-15.

candidate_reported.conflict: Reports disagree on length (6-7 interviews vs up to 10; 2-4 weeks vs ~2 months) and on whether a customer-simulation/presentation round exists.
composite_stages_not_guaranteed: Technical screen HackerRank, completion over Big-O
Onsite: credo behavioral, project-style coding, debugging unfamiliar repo, system design (RAG/ingestion/evals), hiring manager
candidate_reported.bar: Aced: FDE shares SWE technical bar; FDE vs SWE placement often at HM.

gaps: Official process unpublished. Confirm every round with recruiter.

companies.name: Salesforce

role_facts: Company committed to building toward 1,000 FDEs (company statement in the post).
Pods: 1 deployment strategist + 2 FDEs; ~3 months / 1-2 use cases.
Momentum program for nominated customers; paid FDE services planned.
Skills: problem-solving, Apex/JS/prompts/integrations, executive communication, business acumen, learning mindset.
Learning: Trailhead, specialist exams, Agentblazer Legend; new-hire Ready in Six.

candidate_reported.notes: FDEnest groups Salesforce with structured loops plus applied scenario. Not confirmed. Recruiter is the only reliable source.

gaps: Interview round list not published.

companies.name: Indian product companies (Flipkart and peers)

official_process.notes: No Flipkart official round-by-round hiring guide equivalent to Amazon/Microsoft pages was used.

flipkart_common_shape: Machine coding 90-150 min working extensible app plus review
candidate_reported.notes: Machine coding is the closest Indian analog to FDE practical coding. Not a customer-decomposition round. Zoho/Razorpay evidence is thinner and more variable.

companies.fde_titled_loops: Insufficient primary evidence as of access date.

companies.name: Indian IT services (Infosys, TCS, Accenture, and peers)

official_process.notes: Mass-hiring patterns (TCS NQT, InfyTQ, Accenture cognitive/coding) are long-standing public structures but vendor pages were not all fetched as primary PDFs in this pass.

candidate_reported.tcs: NQT foundation + advanced coding for Digital/Prime tracks, then combined TR/MR/HR panel. Depth: projects, OOP, DBMS, SQL, light coding.
candidate_reported.infosys: InfyTQ/HackWithInfy; tracks SE / Specialist Programmer / Power Programmer. Fresher: aptitude, technical, HR.
candidate_reported.accenture: Cognitive + communication + coding for engineering, then technical and HR. Applied AI Engineer Glassdoor hits exist but are not a standard FDE loop.
candidate_reported.genai_partner_fde: SI firms staff GenAI/Agentforce/Databricks partner FDE roles. Interviews usually client-scenario + platform knowledge + mild coding. Evidence quality is low. Confirm whether the loop is the vendor's or the SI's.

certifications_roi.principle: For FDE/GenAI at Palantir, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, a cert almost never substitutes for a shipped system. Certs help ATS screens at enterprises and SIs, structured learning, and JDs that list them. Blog salary-premium claims are not causal evidence.

higher_roi.name: AWS Solutions Architect Associate
higher_roi.employer: high in AWS shops and SIs

higher_roi.name: AWS ML Engineer Associate (MLA-C01) / current ML path
Azure AI Engineer (AI-102 or successor)
higher_roi.learning: high for Azure OpenAI / AI Foundry

higher_roi.name: GCP Professional ML Engineer or Professional Cloud Architect
Databricks Data Engineer / Generative AI Engineer Associate
higher_roi.employer: high for Databricks FDE/RSA and partners; low at Palantir/OpenAI

higher_roi.name: Certified Kubernetes Administrator
higher_roi.employer: medium_high for platform/SRE; medium for FDE

higher_roi.name: NVIDIA NCP-GENL / NCP-AAI (Agentic AI new) / NCP infra exams
higher_roi.employer: medium for GPU infra and NVIDIA partners; low at labs
higher_roi.notes: NCP-AII/AIO are infra ops, not FDE software. DLI course certificates are not NCP exams. NCP-AAI listed as coming soon/new on official pages.

low_roi.name: AWS Cloud Practitioner / Azure AI-900 / GCP Digital Leader
low_roi.why: Foundational multiple-choice; not treated as signal by Palantir/labs/FAANG hiring managers.

low_roi.name: Five-plus associate certs with no production
low_roi.why: Signals exam studying. Target JDs ask for experience.

low_roi.name: Salesforce Agentblazer ranks as a substitute for a portfolio
low_roi.why: Official FDE blog lists Trailhead as skill acquisition, not a hiring exam.

low_roi.name: Generic Coursera/Udemy GenAI professional certificates
low_roi.why: No employer standard; not listed on target-company official hiring pages reviewed.

low_roi.name: NVIDIA DLI workshop badges without NCP
low_roi.why: Course receipt, not professional cert. NVIDIA distinguishes DLI vs NCP.

certifications_roi.fde_rule_of_thumb: One cloud associate in the customer's cloud plus Databricks or Salesforce if that is the platform. A second cloud cert is usually worse than one production-ish RAG/agent with evals.

toy: ChatGPT wrapper around a public PDF with no evals, auth, or deployment story
Tutorial-clone RAG with a README that only says built a RAG app
Notebook-only experiments with no API, tests, or failure analysis
Certificate screenshots as the GitHub hero
recruiter_worthy_mid: One customer-shaped problem with user and success metric
Architecture: retrieval, tools/MCP, orchestration, serving, runtime
Evals: golden set and failure taxonomy
At least two OWASP LLM Top 10 mitigations actually implemented
3-minute walkthrough (slides for OpenAI onsite if asked)
senior: Cloud-AI-platform migration with cost and latency numbers
Multi-agent system with permissioning, audit, and a killed feature
Evidence of changing a customer workflow, plus a failure story
